subject: Reserved capacity imbalance — customer throughput & latency report
messages:
From: Lina Ortega <lina.ortega@finpay.com>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.ai, ops@finpay.com
Date: Sun, 08 Nov 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: High tail latency & 429s on reserved endpoints

Camila —

We started seeing a sustained rise in tail latency and a growing number of 429/503 errors against our reserved endpoints around 15:00 PST today. Throughput has dropped ~18% for our production route and queue depth is spiking; attached are the last 24h p95/p99 charts and a CSV with per-minute success/fail counts.

Impact: checkout flows are timing out for a small percentage of users (2–3%), but that’s enough to trigger banking reconciliation failures on our side. We’re on a committed reserved plan and this is causing an urgent operational impact.

Can you confirm whether this is a capacity saturation in your dedicated pool or an application-level regression? We’d like a mitigation timeline and whether we can temporarily route traffic to a hosted fallback while this is resolved.

Thanks,
Lina Ortega
Head of Platform Reliability, FinPay

Attachments: finpay_latency_1111.png, finpay_throughput_11-08.csv
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Lina Ortega <lina.ortega@finpay.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 09:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: High tail latency & 429s on reserved endpoints

Lina — thanks for the quick heads-up and for the charts; I’ve pulled the attachments and escalated this to our on-call ops and capacity leads. Short answers up front:

- We’re seeing evidence of queue buildup in your assigned reserved pool (pool-id: rsvd-23-east) consistent with an imbalance between incoming QPS and pinned throughput.
- Immediate mitigation options: (1) short-term burst allocation to the dedicated pool (minutes), (2) temporary soft-fallback to our hosted variant for non-sensitive routes, or (3) connection-level retries with exponential backoff client side.

I’m pushing for option (1) + (2) in parallel to minimize customer impact. Can you confirm whether any subset of your traffic is PCI-sensitive today (we need that to know if hosted fallback is allowable)? Also please paste a recent 5-min rate for the route /v1/generate (exact RPS).

We’ll follow up within 2 hours with an ETA for the burst and a proposed rollback window. Apologies for the disruption — we’ll take ownership until this is fully resolved.

—Camila

From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 09:21:00 -0800
Subject: URGENT: FinPay reserved pool imbalance — need immediate capacity/ops actions

Team — Lina from FinPay reports p99 latency rising and 429s for their reserved endpoints (pool rsvd-23-east). Quick facts from their charts + internal signals:
- Measured token throughput demand: ~27k tokens/s sustained over 10m (their committed capacity 32k t/s, but effective throughput dropping due to queueing and headroom policies).
- Queue depth for rsvd-23-east up 4x vs baseline, tail latency p99 ~1.8s (normally ~0.4s).
- Observed error class: transient 429s from admission controller + occasional 503s from serving proxies.

Immediate asks:
1) Rishi — can you open a burst for rsvd-23-east (add 20% headroom) and relax admission thresholds for 30 minutes? If GPUs are pinned, can we borrow from pool rsvd-20-east for the window?
2) Marissa — please prepare a short customer note (30–45m) with two options: (A) temporary hosted fallback for non-PCI routes (needs customer approval), (B) credit + committed SLA remediation offer if we can’t meet short-term throughput. Lina is sensitive to outages; we should lead with option A.
3) Priyom — engineering: look at recent kernel scheduling changes and batching config pushed last week; identify any regression that could have reduced effective throughput (quantization or KV-cache eviction anomalies).

I’ve attached the customer CSV and a draft mitigation memo (sla-mitigation-proposal-draft.pdf). I’m pinging the on-call infra channel: slack://channel/ops-incident — please post progress there so we have a single source of truth.

Thanks — need updates ASAP.
—Camila
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Lina Ortega <lina.ortega@finpay.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: High tail latency & 429s on reserved endpoints — remediation plan and timeline

Lina — quick update and plan. Appreciate your patience. Summary of actions we executed and next steps: 

What we observed (short): dedicated pool rsvd-23-east entered a transient saturation window driven by a burst of long-context requests + reduced batching efficiency after a config change earlier this week. That caused queue amplification and admission rejections (429).

Actions taken (completed):
- +25% short-term burst applied to rsvd-23-east at 09:36 PST (Rishi) — reduced queue depth by ~60% within 7 minutes.
- Temporarily relaxed admission thresholds and enabled cross-pool borrow from rsvd-20-east for stateless requests.
- Rolled back last-week batching kernel tweak on a canary subset to restore prior batching behavior (Priyom).

Customer impact mitigation (next 2–4 hrs):
- We recommend routing non-PCI traffic to our hosted fallback for up to 4 hours to fully drain queues and validate steady-state throughput. If you approve, we can flip a soft-route in 15–20 minutes and monitor p99 closely.
- We will run an extended regression test against your production prompt set and provide a follow-up report by EOD today.

Executive note: Marissa will follow up with a compensation proposal if we do not meet the committed SLA for the affected window. We’ve also tagged this for a post-mortem to prevent recurrence and are prioritizing a permanent autoscaling rule change for reserved pools.

Please reply with: (A) approval for hosted fallback for non-PCI routes, and (B) the list of any PCI-sensitive routes that must stay on dedicated. If we don’t hear back in 30 minutes we’ll provision the fallback for low-risk routes to avoid further customer impact.

Again, apologies — we’ll stay on this until fully resolved.

—Camila Reyes
Account Lead, Strategic Sales | Redwood Inference
Cc: Marissa Cole (VP, Customer Success), Rishi Malhotra (Capacity Lead), Priyom Das (SRE)

Attachments referenced: sla-mitigation-proposal-draft.pdf
